Wen Ti, as a remonstrating official acting at others' direction, factionally shielded revenge and confused the censorate, and therefore memorialized: "Kang Youwei was previously unknown to me when he suddenly came to my door seeking an audience and presented his writings; reading them, I found reform to be his doctrine.

Wen Ti, holding that remonstrating officials were directed by others, engaged in factional shielding and revenge, and threw the censorate into disorder, therefore memorialized: "Kang Youwei was previously unknown to me when he suddenly came to my door seeking an audience and presented his writings; reading them, I found reform to be his doctrine.

以言官為人指使，黨庇報復，紊亂臺諫 gives Wen Ti’s grounds—that censors were directed by others, practiced factional shielding and revenge, and disordered the censorate—not that Wen Ti himself acted at others’ direction. The proposal’s agent fix is right, but “directed by others in factional shielding and revenge that confused…” collapses the three parallel predicates awkwardly; keep them coordinated.
